text: Five defects neither the author nor CI would have caught, and one refutation of a reviewer by the other. Both seats received the frozen diff and the author's claims as CLAIMS, not facts, and both returned CHANGES-REQUIRED. The most valuable finding was not a bug in the code but a lie in its prose: the file called itself blocking while sitting in no required context — the exists-!=-armed disease reproduced inside the very file written to cure it.

what: Calling the job blocking is dishonest: with no branch-protection requirement a red run does not stop a merge.
cure: header now says SIGNAL-ONLY UNTIL PROMOTED and names the promotion as an operator-gated repo-settings action tracked in PENDING-ARMS

what: Claimed the second apt-get call was missing sudo.
cure: none needed — the diff reads `sudo apt-get update -qq && sudo apt-get install -y -qq zsh`, and the run on head fc46300838 succeeded, which it could not have done had the claim been true. The other seat independently reached the same conclusion and called it a non-finding. Recorded rather than dropped: a refuter's HIGH is a claim like any other.

what: cancel-in-progress keyed on github.ref cancels in-flight main runs, so a later push silently suppresses an alarm from the run before it. The merge_group clause is vacuous here.
cure: cancel-in-progress is now scoped to pull_request events only

what: Judging by exit code alone cannot see the corpus SHRINKING: if checks silently disappear while the survivors pass, the run stays green.
cure: a floor assertion on the printed check count, added IN ADDITION to the exit code — an absent TOTAL line is itself an error, so an aborted setup cannot pass as a satisfied floor

what: Node is unpinned, so a runner-image bump can flip this job red or change probe behaviour with no repo change to point at.
cure: actions/setup-node pinned; the repo has no .nvmrc, so the version is named in the workflow and the reason recorded

what: The paths filter may miss the probe's import closure — package manifests, shared libraries — so a breaking change would never trigger the job.
cure: measured instead of assumed: the probe imports ONLY node builtins (node:crypto, node:fs, node:os, node:path, node:url), so there is no import closure to widen to. The residue the seats were right about is the Node runtime itself, which is why it is now pinned. Both seats reasoned from the general shape of the risk; the specific file does not carry it.

what: test_voa_probe_corpus.py is named in paths but executed by no step, so a PR editing only the shim gets a green check that tested nothing of it.
cure: not executed — the shim's only job is to invoke the SAME .sh corpus this workflow already runs directly, so a step would double-run it. Kept in paths, with the reason now written in the header instead of left implicit.

what: The workflow file is in the pull_request filter but not the push one, so a direct push to main editing only this file runs nothing.
